articles.title: Coaches Poll Prediction: Just How Hard Will Ohio State, Ole Miss, and LSU Crash?
articles.summary: LSU, Ole Miss, Kentucky, and Ohio State got rocked, and there will be huge moves after these four drop. Here's our Week 11 Coaches Poll prediction.
articles.body:
It's not just that Ohio State, Ole Miss, and LSU lost. It's how that will be why the Week 11 Coaches Poll will see so many big moves. BYU lost, and so did Missouri, but they fought the good fight and won't drop too much. The same goes for No. 1 Miami after its battle with Notre Dame. Kentucky had a rough time, but it lost on the road at Tennessee.

Ohio State got hit with an Oregon tsunami in the 41-28 loss. LSU couldn't keep up with Alabama in a 31-13 blowout, and Ole Miss wasn't even close, getting dunked on 42-7 by Georgia. And here's the real problem for the Buckeyes, Tigers, and Rebels – they all lost at home. Here's our call for what the Week 11 Coaches Poll Top 25 will be. – Predictions: AP Poll | CFP Top 25

2026 Coaches Poll Prediction: Week 11 Quick Hits

Don't expect anything crazy up top. Miami will move down to just behind Notre Dame, and Georgia, Indiana, Utah, UCLA, and the Irish will all move up a slot. However, Utah might jump past IU into the No. 2 spot.

The biggest winners will be: Notre Dame, Texas, Alabama

The biggest losers will be: (besides Ohio State, LSU, and Ole Miss) Miami, Missouri, Northwestern

articles.title: How to watch Chiefs vs. Jets today: Time, TV channel for Week 9
articles.summary: Here's everything you need to know to watch the Kansas City Chiefs face the New York Jets in Week 9 of the 2026 NFL regular season.
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs return to the Show Me State this week to take on the New York Jets at Arrowhead Stadium in Week 9 of the 2026 season.

After relinquishing control of first place in the AFC West to the Denver Broncos last week, the Chiefs will need a strong showing against the Jets if they want to improve their chances of winning the division.

Here's everything fans need to know to watch Kansas City face off against New York this afternoon:

What channel is Chiefs vs. Jets game on today? Time, TV schedule

TV channel: KCTV 5 (CBS) Streaming: NFL+ and Paramount+ Start time: 3:25 p.m. CT Announcers: Jim Nantz (play-by-play), J.J. Watt (analyst) Sideline reporter(s) : Tracy Wolfson

Chiefs vs. Jets radio broadcast: Which station is the game on?

Chiefs Radio Network: 96.5 The Fan (96.5 FM) Play-by-Play: Mitch Holthus Color: Danan Hughes Sideline: Josh Klingler

The Kansas City Chiefs desperately need to bounce back against the Jets after last week's loss to the Denver Broncos. Three straight losses could easily push them out of playoff contention at this point in the season.

The Chiefs got a shot in the arm last week with the return of wide receiver Rashee Rice, but running back Kenneth Walker remains the focal point of the offense. Walker's two-game streak of subpar play has certainly been frustrating, but he will likely return to form this week. New York ranks 21st in the league in rushing yards allowed, which should make for a pretty easy bounce-back game for the reigning Super Bowl MVP.

Kansas City's inability to pressure opposing quarterbacks has been a problem all season, but it is finally starting to catch up with defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo's squad. The Chiefs' secondary can only pick up the slack for so long. The Jets' offensive line has allowed 23 sacks this season, which should give defensive tackle Chris Jones a chance to record his first sack.

articles.title: OGC Nice predicted XI v Angers: Axel Witsel to drop to the bench?

articles.body:
Axel Witsel quickly carved out a place in OGC Nice's midfield since joining over the summer and he has even inherited the captain's armband, however, he may drop to the bench for the visit to SCO Angers this afternoon.

Instead, Olivier Pantaloni may opt for a midfield duo of Hicham Boudaoui and Djibril Coulibaly. It would see the captain's armband handed to Youssouf Ndayishimiye, who is expected to start at the heart of the defence. There are no fresh injury concerns for Pantaloni to contend with, although the likes of Moise Bombito, Antoine Mendy, and Laurent Abergel all remain sidelined with long-term injuries. articles.title: Elversberg take record-breaking crowd to Borussia Dortmund
articles.summary: Elversberg took 8,000 fans to the Signal Iduna Park for their Bundesliga clash against Borussia Dortmund. Although suffering a 2-1 defeat, their fourth in 20...
articles.body:
Elversberg took 8,000 fans to the Signal Iduna Park for their Bundesliga clash against Borussia Dortmund. Although suffering a 2-1 defeat, their fourth in 2026/27, memories will have been created to last a lifetime for generations of Elversberg's travelling contingent.

But what makes the figure more impressive, is that it's a club record for Elversberg, who had never played higher than Germany's 3. Liga until 2023. Additionally, the 8,000 travelling supporters makes up 61 percent of the town's population – it really is that small!

Speaking prior to Elversberg's trip to Elversberg, head coach Vincent Wagner said: "Hooray, the whole community is here."

And despite being 2-0 down thanks to Felix Nmecha's second-half brace , Noel Futkeu's 81st-minute bicycle kick almost kickstarted a comeback.

Defeat at the Signal Iduna Park leaves the Saarland club on 13 points from a possible 27 after nine matchdays, a commendable tally for a club that was playing in Germany's fourth tier in 2022.

articles.title: 'Coach and selectors picked the team': Pakistan captain Babar Azam reveals his real role in Test team ahead SL series
articles.summary: Babar Azam revealed his exact role as captain in the Pakistan Test team ahead of the Sri Lanka series.
articles.body:
Pakistan Test captain Babar Azam says selectors and the coach pick the squad, and he fields the XI.

He admitted he knew nothing about the mid-series overhaul that shook Pakistan in England.

The first Test against Sri Lanka starts in Rawalpindi on 9 November.

Pakistan vs Sri Lanka 1st Test: Babar Azam explains captain's role in team selection

Pakistan Test captain Babar Azam has spelt out how little say he has in squad selection decisions, just as a new home series begins against Sri Lanka on November 9 in Rawalpindi.

Previously, during the England tour this summer, when Pakistan lost the first two Tests, on the eve of the third Test at Edgbaston, the PCB ordered a sweeping change in which seven players were sent home, and two members of the coaching staff were removed.

Those affected included senior names such as Mohammad Rizwan and Imam-ul-Haq, as well as all-rounder Aamir Jamal and young batter Awais Zafar, who returned without playing a match. Reports said that the players learned about it through social media and press releases, with no direct word from the captain, head coach or PCB officials beforehand.

Former captain and national selector Misbah-ul-Haq reportedly resigned from the selection committee in protest, after confirming that nobody had consulted him about the seven recalled players.

Babar was asked before the Edgbaston Test whether he had been told about the changes, and he said that he had not.

"No, it was news for me too. I also came to know about this later. But as I said earlier, the PCB made this decision. I think they will explain it better," he said.

What did Babar Azam say about his involvement in Pakistan squad selection?

Before facing Sri Lanka, a journalist asked why Abdullah Fazal, who had been the first-choice opener in the West Indies, had now been left out, and spinner Sajid Khan had also been omitted.

Babar began his reply by accepting that it was a fair question and then pointed to what had happened in England.

"Ever since we returned from England, the scenario that unfolded has been right in front of you," he said.

He went on to describe how the squad for the new series was put together and where his own duties begin.

"When we sat down for this squad, the 15 players selected and provided to me by the selectors and the coach; my job is to field the playing XI from that group, get performances out of them, and have them fight out on the field. As for the rest, that is not in my hands," he told the media.

The captain then drew a clear line between the squad and the match-day team, and explained that he did not wish to go through every detail in public.

"Selection is their job; that's their domain," Babar said. "Where my responsibility is, I'll state it. Wherever I have a say, I certainly provide my input. Ultimately, the selectors, the coach, and I sit together to discuss, and we do whatever is best possible."

Babar's answer protects him, but it leaves questions over who is accountable

Babar's reply was careful and, on the face of it, fair, because a captain who is handed 15 players can only pick from them. However, it throws light on how the captain is kept afar from team selections.

Pakistan had a bruising England tour in which the players were left to read about their own removal online, and the person who leads the team on the field was also in the dark.

That points to a bigger problem than any single selection. If the captain does not know about decisions as large as a seven-player overhaul, and a selector like Misbah says he was not asked either, then it is not clear who is responsible when things go wrong.

The line "selection is their job" is true, but it also shows how far the captain stands from the choices that define his side.

For Babar, the best response is on the field. A captain who delivers runs and wins in Rawalpindi will find it easier to argue for a greater role in the next selection meeting. The PCB, meanwhile, needs to explain its process openly so that players hear about their futures from the board, not from their phones.

articles.title: The missing piece that Roberto De Zerbi must slot into place after Tottenham's puzzling start
articles.summary: De Zerbi must find a way to turn around the fortunes of Spurs’ underperforming forward line to create the optimum attacking formula
articles.body:
Tottenham arrived at Elland Road with three consecutive wins and departed disappointed by their failings in three departments. "We did not show character, we did not show personality, we did not show courage," lamented Roberto De Zerbi and, if he was discussing the second half at Leeds, they amounted to fundamental failings for him.

The temptation is to take a swipe at the forward line and say they were found wanting in three other areas: left winger, right winger and centre-forward. That is probably unfair on Mohammed Kudus , a considerable talent only a few starts into a comeback, and cruel to Mathys Tel , taken off before half-time with what De Zerbi fears is a bad injury.

Spurs can argue that picking on those charged with scoring is harsh, given that they had seven goals from their three previous games before a powderpuff attack barely threatened Leeds. But the facts show that only Nottingham Forest, Crystal Palace and Sunderland have scored fewer in the Premier League - and that may change after Sunday's games.

Only three of Spurs' 10 have come from forwards: Dominic Solanke 's injury-time equaliser at Old Trafford, Omar Marmoush's thunderbolt against Coventry and Tel's glorious solo goal at Chelsea. A case of quality rather than quantity, perhaps, even if they could all be damned by comparisons with the Ballon d'Or winner who used to deliver both for Spurs; that said, Harry Kane is on a four-game goal drought for Bayern Munich.

It may be one of the few ways that Marmoush, whose own drought spans a mere three matches, ranks better than Kane. Yet the Egyptian is the face of a conundrum Spurs have created with their record outlay; while those three victories offered encouraging evidence that De Zerbi's buys are having an impact in defence and midfield, the attacking acquisitions were Marmoush and Savio, who have a combined tally of one goal and no assists in the top flight. The Brazilian has not played for four weeks but, between them, they will earn Manchester City £145m. City seem to have got much the better of those deals.

Savio has always faced the question of whether he can be productive enough and if he is best suited to the left or the right, Kudus' best position. Marmoush increasingly faces the question of what he is: neither really a striker nor a winger. The Egyptian was prolific for Eintracht Frankfurt in a strike duo, alongside Hugo Ekitike; but De Zerbi does not play two up front. Solanke, more of a conventional spearhead, has four goals in his last 25 league games.

Tottenham have a host of imperfect options on the left – Savio, Tel, Marmoush – and if the 18-year-old Luca Williams-Barnett can generate the most excitement, that is in part an indictment of others when he has only played nine minutes of first-team football.

Is De Zerbi closer to finding his optimum attacking formula? It does not feel so, even if that is not entirely his fault. An ever-changing cast list is part of the complication. So is the question of the specialist No 10s, who all started the season injured and are on various points of the comeback trail; but then it is unsure if De Zerbi's system will always contain one.

He played more of a 4-3-3 at Leeds, with Archie Gray as a No 8. If Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes, the £185m double act who have become the club's two most expensive signings, excelled in alliance with each other at Chelsea, there is the unresolved issue if De Zerbi uses them with a more defensive midfielder, such as Rodrigo Bentancur, a No 8 or a No 10. Fernandes and Conor Gallagher, each more of a No 8 by trade, have played in the more advanced roles at times this season.

All of which could create congestion for a position that is sometimes obsolete. Of the players who seem to belong in Tottenham's truest traditions, Xavi Simons is back in training, James Maddison scored a lovely goal against Coventry but, after missing training for some of the week, went unused at Leeds, and Dejan Kulusevski had his longest outing for 17 months, with 25 minutes.

Each might sprinkle a little magic; some would have been welcome at Leeds. Tottenham could be more creative; perhaps should be, having added classier passers in the middle of midfield. But they rank in mid-table for some of the chance creation and shooting statistics.

They have fared particularly badly in two: as the last team in the country to score a league goal and even now, with their 10, with a shot conversion rate of 6.5 percent. The figures would be worse but for their unlikely top scorer: defender Jan Paul van Hecke, who has two goals from 11 shots.

If others strip him of that status, and with games against Ipswich, Sunderland and Fulham next, there is the chance for Spurs to win six games out of seven. But even accounting for the oddities of their season, that surely requires some goals from the attackers who are usually responsible for scoring them.

articles.title: Messi becomes first player to win back-to-back MLS Golden Boot awards
articles.summary: The Argentinian scored 26 goals in regular season, topping the charts and leading Inter Miami to the MLS Cup playoffs.
articles.body:
Lionel Messi has become the first player to win back-to-back Golden Boot awards in Major League Soccer after leading his club Inter Miami to a second-place finish in the Eastern Conference.

MLS defending champions Miami earned a wasteful 3-3 draw against Charlotte on the final day of the regular season on Saturday.

The Argentinian superstar did not score but set up the first two goals at Miami’s Nu Stadium, both from corners, to help secure home advantage for his club in the first two playoff rounds.

Ian Fray, Luis Suarez and Rodrigo De Paul racked up three first-half strikes for Inter Miami before Liel Abada’s brace soon after the break led to a comeback sealed by Rodolfo Aloko’s late strike.

Runaway overall leaders Nashville broke the all-time MLS points record for a season with a whopping 77 after beating Cincinnati 2-0. At 23-3 with eight draws, Nashville won the East and broke the mark of 74 points set by Miami in 2024.

Miami finished second in the East on 60 points as third-place New England failed to take advantage of Inter’s draw with a surprise 1-0 loss at Orlando to end on 58.

At Miami, Messi’s 14th-minute corner fell unexpectedly to Charlotte’s Luca de la Torre, who spooned it up for Fray to open the scoring.

Another Messi corner in the 33rd minute found Suarez wide open at the near post. The Uruguayan glanced in his header for 2-0.

De Paul made it three before half-time, but Abada pulled back a goal for the visitors early and bagged a second in the 55th minute.

In the 90th minute, Aloko bagged the equaliser, reacting first to the ball as Smalls’s shot ricocheted off the post.

A visibly frustrated Messi hit the post in stoppage time before Aloko came inches from bagging an unlikely winner with a thunderous shot into the outside netting.

Messi’s 26 goals this season were enough to make him the first to successfully defend the top goal-scoring honour. Petar Musa of Dallas was second with 22 goals but did not score in his club’s 3-1 home victory over Colorado.

The 39-year-old finished with 29 goals the previous season, becoming the second player in league ⁠⁠⁠⁠history to score at ⁠⁠⁠⁠least 25 times in back-to-back years.

Messi recently retired from international football after an illustrious 21-year career with the 2022 world champions, but recently signed a contract extension ⁠⁠with the MLS club through 2028.

Inter Miami are the holders of the MLS Cup, which they won in Messi’s second season with the club in 2025.

Playoffs for this season’s MLS Cup begin ‌‌on November 19.

Messi’s men will face Columbus to begin the MLS playoffs. Other East matchups send New England against Philadelphia, Charlotte against Chicago and top seed Nashville against the wild-card winner, Orlando or Cincinnati.

Columbus took advantage of the Cincinnati loss with a 4-3 victory at Chicago to finish seventh and avoid the wild-card round.

articles.title: 4 Trade Ideas for Erik Karlsson and the Pittsburgh Penguins Amid NHL Rumors
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Penguins were one of the NHL's biggest surprises during the 2025-26 season, snapping what had been a three-year playoff drought and overcoming pretty much every preseason expectation that had them projected as a lottery team.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Penguins were one of the NHL's biggest surprises during the 2025-26 season, snapping what had been a three-year playoff drought and overcoming pretty much every preseason expectation that had them projected as a lottery team.

It was the perfect combination of future Hall of Famers finding the fountain of youth, pretty much every offseason move (and in-season move) working out better than expected, and some young players showing they were maybe ahead of schedule in their development (specifically, 2025 first-round pick Ben Kindel).

Now a little more than a month into the 2026-27 season, things are not going as smoothly.

Some of the veteran players are showing their age; some of the offseason moves have not worked out as well as in the summer of 2025; the power play has been awful, all while the defense has struggled and the young goalies are struggling to find consistency at the NHL level.

The result, so far, has been that the team is at the bottom of the Eastern Conference standings and the NHL standings.

It has also accelerated trade speculation around the team, especially as it relates to some of their veteran players, some of whom are in the final year of their current deals.

There is still a lot of hockey to be played, and there is enough talent here and enough wild cards on the roster that it is possible to think it could still turn around. It may not be time to completely panic just yet. But they do have to be realistic about their situation. It is the very early stages of a rebuild. They enter play on Sunday with just six wins in their first 17 games. In the salary cap era (going back to the start of the 2005-06 season), only 19 teams that have won six games or fewer within their first 17 games of a season have actually made the playoffs in that season. There have been 106 that missed. The odds are not really in their favor.

So let's try to look at some of the players that could be moved, the challenges that could come from moving them, and try to piece together some ideas and suggestions.

There is going to be a lot of incentive for the Penguins to make some trades at some point this season.

Maybe not immediately, but based on where they are in the standings, the hurdles they have in front of them this season, a desire to keep adding more young players and assets, and the fact that they have some younger players who have probably earned at least a look in the NHL who are currently blocked.

The problem: Some of the players they might want to trade are not going to be easy to trade.

Sidney Crosby, Evgeni Malkin and Kris Letang have been their big three for two decades, and they may not want to leave Pittsburgh. The Penguins' new owners may not want them to leave Pittsburgh, either. All three have no-movement clauses in their contracts, while Letang simply may not have a lot of value given the term remaining and how he is not the player he once was.

Erik Karlsson is a pending free agent after this season, but can also dictate where (or if) he goes.

Rickard Rakell has a 10-team no-trade clause.

Rakell and Bryan Rust are both mid-30s wingers with term remaining on their contracts beyond this season. Mid-30s wingers with term are generally some of the least desirable trade assets on the market, and not many teams are beating down the door to acquire them.

Andrei Kuzmenko and Sam Girard are unrestricted free agents after the season with no trade restrictions, but their play really has not been at a level that will generate interest.

Justin Brazeau could be attractive as a depth piece given his cheap contract, lack of term, and strong season a year ago.

So it is going to be complicated. But let's see if we can come up with some ideas anyway. It is also unlikely that all of these players go. Or even more than one. Even though the Penguins would no doubt like to make some moves, and even though they are in a rebuild, it does not seem like the type of rebuild that is going to see them sell off everybody and tear it all down to the studs. But there still could (and should) be some moves in the coming weeks and months.

The trade idea: Bruins trade forward Matthew Poitras and the later of their two 2027 first-round picks to Pittsburgh for Erik Karlsson.

The Bruins are off to a sensational start to the 2026-27 season and seem to have a significantly better process behind that success than they did a year ago. They have some really high-end players who can be game-changers, and with James Hagens and Fraser Minten starting to make an impact, there is finally some youth and fresh talent making an impact.

What they could use is a little more offensive spark from their blue line.

Karlsson is still searching for a Stanley Cup, and while Boston may not be the best contender in the Eastern Conference right now, it's still looking like a playoff team that has an elite forward (David Pastrnak), a legit top-pairing defenseman (Charlie McAvoy) and a franchise goalie (Jeremy Swayman). That is a team that could do some damage and make some noise. Karlsson may not be the three-time Norris Trophy winner he was at his peak, but he showed last year he can still play at an extremely high level with the right players around him and in the right situation.

Maybe this could be that type of situation and strengthen the Bruins' chances.

The idea: Sharks trade a conditional first-round pick (top-10 protected this year) to the Penguins for Bryan Rust.

Even though the Sharks have a ton of young talent, it is a team that still has a lot of holes and a long way to go before it is a contender.

It is a team that needs to learn how to win.

It is also a team that has absolutely zero depth beyond Macklin Celebrini, and entering play on Sunday, it has been outscored by a 12-28 margin without him on the ice during 5-on-5 play.

It is a team that not only needs more scoring depth, but it is also a team that needs something of a veteran presence, and somebody who can bring some seriousness and winning experience to it. Rust would be a great veteran to add to that group, and he could play a variety of roles up and down the lineup. The biggest issue at the moment is that Rust is sidelined due to injury, so something like this would have to be a later-season deal after he gets back.

Terrible Contracts Teams Wish They Could Dump 🤦‍♂️

The idea: Penguins trade forward Justin Brazeau, a second-round pick, and a fifth-round pick to the Capitals for Ivan Miroshnichenko.

The trade ideas do not have to be about the Penguins necessarily selling.

They could also be in the market to add players, especially if they are young.

The Penguins have spent the better part of the past two years taking fliers on young players who have needed a change of scenery from their previous teams, in the hopes that they can catch lightning in a bottle with them. They have had varying degrees of success with it. Some of the players they have taken chances on include Egor Chinakhov, Kaeden Korczak, Nicholas Robertson, Elmer Soderblom, and even Hendrix Lapierre, who they acquired from the Capitals early in the offseason, fits that mold.

Maybe they could go back to the Capitals again, because Miroshnichenko could also fit into that template they have been trying to follow. Especially if they move out somebody like a Rust or Rakell to open up a roster spot in a different trade.

The Capitals would like a first-round pick for him, but that seems like a steep price for a player who is 22 years old and hasn't quite panned out.

Chinakhov was a more established player when the Penguins traded for him a year ago, and that only cost them Danton Heinen, a second-round pick, and another mid-round pick.

So let's look at something like that as the model here.

The idea: Canadiens trade defenseman Adam Engstrom and a second-round pick to Pittsburgh for Rickard Rakell.

Montreal has one of the best young core groups of talent in the NHL, and after reaching the Eastern Conference Final a year ago, there are major expectations for them to compete for a championship starting this season.

There is reason to believe they are capable of it.

As good as their roster is, they could definitely use another top-nine forward, and while a center is their biggest need, Rakell would still be an intriguing target for them given his versatility. He has played a little bit of center over the past two years for the Penguins, and has more than held his own in that spot. He's also a very good winger with some creativity and a better-than-advertised two-way game that has also seen him take on some penalty-killing role for the Penguins this season.

He had a horrible start to the season from a goal-scoring perspective, but he was still creating chances and just seemed to be a little snakebit when it came to finishing. That has started to turn around for him. He is signed through the end of next season at a very reasonable $5 million per year salary cap number.

Mid-30s wingers are not usually high on a team's trade target lists, but Rakell's ability to play different roles could make him a little more attractive.

articles.title: How to Watch Cowboys vs. Colts: TV Channel, Live Stream, Time
articles.summary: Cowboys vs. Colts kicks off Sunday, Nov. 8, at 1 p.m. ET on FOX. Get the players to watch for this Week 9 game in Indianapolis.

articles.title: Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup: Wales captain Boyd-Ward to make 50-cap history
articles.summary: Jodie Boyd-Ward will become the first player in Wheelchair Rugby League history to win 50 caps when she leads Wales against New Zealand.
articles.body:
Wales captain Jodie Boyd-Ward is to become the first player in Wheelchair Rugby League history to win 50 caps.

The Leeds Rhinos skipper will lead Wales in their World Cup fifth-place play-off semi-final against New Zealand in Wollongong on Monday (00:00 GMT).

Boyd-Ward will be winning her 21st Wales cap, having also played 22 times for England and seven times for Ireland.

Wales' top goal-scorer Andrew Higgins will hope to add to his tally of 158 goals as he joins leading try-scorer Stuart Williams (77) in winning a 40th Wales cap.

Meanwhile, father and son Martin and Matthew Turner will play together for the first time, a Wales landmark at a World Cup.

The match will also be the first between Wales and New Zealand in the wheelchair version of the sport.

News and reports on the BBC Sport website

Sid Ramsey and Mark Williams earn recalls in the wake of Wales' 92-18 win against the United States, their first at the tournament.

"Jodie reaching 50 international caps is an absolutely incredible achievement," said Wales head coach Alan Caron.

"To be the first player in the world to reach that milestone in Wheelchair Rugby League, and the first female to do so, is something very special. She deserves enormous credit for everything she has contributed to the sport.

"It's also particularly pleasing to have Martin and Matthew together in the side; it's great that they'll finally get the chance to play alongside each other for Wales for the first time."

articles.title: India gets its 100th Grandmaster! Anuj Shrivatri becomes first GM from Madhya Pradesh
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Anuj Shrivatri of Madhya Pradesh became India’s 100th chess Grandmaster on Sunday, completing the title requirements by winning the 7th ASEAN
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Anuj Shrivatri of Madhya Pradesh became India’s 100th chess Grandmaster on Sunday, completing the title requirements by winning the 7th ASEAN Plus Individual Open Chess Championship. The result also made him the first Grandmaster from his state.Shrivatri, born in 2004, began the tournament with a loss. He lost his opening game, then recovered to finish on seven points after nine rounds.That was half a point clear of Vietnam’s Nguyen Duc Hoa, with Nouri Alekhine of the Philippines third on six.The title was still in the balance in the closing rounds, and he won the last two with everything at stake.The result came on Diwali, the festival of light.The milestone ends a wait that began in 1988, when Viswanathan Anand became India’s first Grandmaster.The country has added several in recent months, with S Aswath becoming the 98th in July and VS Rathanvel the 99th more recently.Shrivatri had been among the names touted as the likely 100th.He has long been seen as a prospect. Shrivatri earned the IM title in 2020 and was then reported to be the youngest International Master from Madhya Pradesh. Six years on, the next step is complete.For Indian chess, the number carries symbolic weight. India has had the 100th Grandmaster title in sight for some time, and the speed at which new Grandmasters have arrived shows how strong the country’s talent pipeline has become.For Madhya Pradesh, which had not produced one until now, Shrivatri’s name opens a new chapter.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ale Galán: "En 2027 Chingalán sigue y con equipo nuevo"
articles.standfirst: El español atiende a MARCA para hablar de su lesión, la ausencia en el Mundial, la continuidad de la pareja dos y de un futuro en el que se plantea “ser el primero en ser número también en la derecha”
articles.summary: El español atiende a MARCA para hablar de su lesión, la ausencia en el Mundial, la continuidad de la pareja dos y de un futuro en el que se plantea “ser el primero en ser número también en la derecha”
articles.body: Ale Galán (Madrid, España, 1996) es el nombre del momento en el pádel mundial. Por exceso o defecto, el español se ha convertido en el epicentro de la atención mundial del deporte de la pala en el mejor momento de su carrera deportiva al tener que perderse, primero, el Major de Kuwait y el Mundial con España, después, por una lesión en la mano derecha que lejos de las especulaciones se hizo en pista intentando una recuperación en Milán. Por primera vez Galán abre las puertas de su casa a un medio y lo hace en un día muy especial, el de la final del Mundial. En las horas previas a la gran cita mundialista atiende a MARCA para hablar sin líneas rojas de todos los temas que orbitan entorno a su figura y lo hace con una pose cercana, relajada y más madura de lo habitual que recupera parte de la normalidad que un chico de Leganés que despuntó pronto y rápido en el deporte perdió durante años obligado, quizá, a protegerse de una exposición excesiva. A punto de ser padre por primera vez, el exnúmero uno se sabe afortunado. No se conforma y es ambicioso, pero tampoco parece obsesionado con volver a ser número uno y afronta las dudas y miedos (lesión, críticas, rumores o frustración) que se le han planteado en los últimos meses con una naturalidad que las grandes estrellas de la pala, como era de esperar ante la atención que ya generan, están perdiendo. El mismo camino en etapas diferentes, vaya. Galán, cumplidos ya los 30, afronta un proyecto nuevo por primera vez en su carrera y lo hará, sí, con Fede Chingotto. El proyecto Chingalán se mantiene al menos un año más porque sigue creyendo en que puede conseguir lo que tantas temporadas se le ha resistido y, cuando acabe su era, Galán ya tiene objetivos en mente para la era post. Y no por lógicos dejan de sorprender. Pregunta: Lo primero agradecerte que nos abras las puertas de tu casa en un momento como este y para comenzar creo que todo el mundo del pádel quiere saber cómo estás. Ale Galán: Bueno, esta es la peor parte, la de perderme este tipo de momentos. Tampoco quiero ser el protagonista; creo que hoy es el día de los jugadores de la Selección y ojalá sea un gran día para ellos. Mi papel hoy es contarte mi experiencia y vivirlo desde aquí, desde casa. P: Preguntarte cómo estás es más que obvio viéndote con esa férula de inmovilización. ¿Cómo evoluciona? A.G.: Sí, es la recomendación médica en este tipo de tratamiento conservador para mantener la mano inmovilizada y que pueda cicatrizar lo antes posible. Para generar el menor riesgo posible, la mantengo inmovilizada. P: Hablaremos de la lesión más adelante, pero hoy es un día muy especial para el pádel en general. Sea uno español o argentino, es la final que todo el mundo quería ver y disfrutar. Tú seguro que también quieres disfrutarla, pero no desde la posición que te habría gustado. ¿Cómo se vive tener que ponerse delante de la televisión a ver algo donde serías uno de los grandes protagonistas? A.G.: Da un poco de nostalgia porque esta sensación es nueva para mí. Nunca he estado lesionado ni he visto un Mundial desde casa. Ha sido difícil seguirlo desde esta posición, pero me deja tranquilo el equipo que hay. Eso me hizo poner en la balanza que tenemos un gran equipo para ganar y tomar la decisión de descansar. Ojalá sea con victoria hoy, pero sí, es un momento bastante agrio. La lesión es algo que va adherido al deporte, le pasa a muchos jugadores y en esta ocasión me toca vivirlo a mí. P: La decisión de no ir al Mundial, ¿ha sido la más dura del año o incluso de tu carrera? El Mundial siempre es muy especial para los jugadores y, estando el número uno definido al no poder ir a Kuwait, no tuvo que ser fácil decir que no a la Selección. A.G.: Totalmente. En cuestión de decisión sí ha sido la más difícil. Estuvo sobre la mesa jugar de la forma que pudiera, pero eso iba a ocasionar tener que operarme. En la balanza estaba una fecha señalada como el Mundial, que pasa cada dos años y al que iba con muchas ganas de revancha tras la anterior edición, frente a tener paciencia y tratar de volver lo mejor posible al cien por cien de cara a todo lo que viene. Aunque sea de los mayores del circuito, como suelo decir, quiero que me queden muchos años de carrera y no quería asumir tanto riesgo. Tampoco soy una pieza imprescindible porque tenemos un equipazo y ojalá hoy podamos celebrar la victoria con ellos. P: ¿Te atreves a dar un pronóstico para la final? A.G.: Yo creo que va a ganar España. Creo que cambia la estrategia y que el foco hay que tenerlo en ganar dos partidos. Es más fácil mantenerlo así que tratando de tener todas las parejas completas. Hay equipo para ganar dos partidos, que al final es lo que importa en el Mundial, y así ganamos en 2021. P: ¿Ves a España ganando en dos o en tres partidos? A.G.: Eso es una estrategia de los entrenadores, cómo quieren plantearlo y dónde colocar sus parejas más fuertes. Dependerá del orden de las parejas. Yo creo que buscando las dos parejas más fuertes de España, esos dos partidos se pueden ganar contra cualquiera. En este momento me parece que, por una cuestión de ranking, Argentina tiene un equipo más completo y llega en un muy buen momento, pero España tiene lo necesario para ganar dos partidos. Ya sean dos o tres, lo que importa es acabar ganándolos. P: ¿Has hablado con tus compañeros o con el seleccionador esta semana, o te mantienes al margen? A.G.: El equipo tiene su propio chat interno. Todos me pusieron un mensaje muy cariñoso por privado y en el grupo, y les he dejado organizarse. Con los que más relación tengo, por supuesto que he mantenido el contacto. P: Se te nota triste al hablar de ello. ¿Te planteaste ir como segundo capitán, parte de la expedición o como aficionado? A.G.: Yo expresé el deseo de estar. Cuando estaba la duda y viajaba entre Barcelona y Madrid hablando con médicos, le dije a la Federación que mi deseo era jugar, y si no, estar allí. Se puso sobre la mesa, pero lo más inteligente para el equipo era tener a un jugador top sano. Se echa de menos porque es un torneo diferente por equipos donde compartes con compañeros y rivales en dinámicas de grupo. Tenía la fecha señalada y me he hartado de hablar del Mundial todo el año, pero hay que aceptar el momento. P: Tu ausencia impide ver un cruce hipotético en la final entre los número uno (Coello y Tapia) y los número dos (Chingotto y Galán) cruzando parejas. De haber estado, ¿cómo habrías planteado la alineación? A.G.: Si hablamos del hipotético de jugar Arturo y yo juntos, ya hemos jugado en alguna ocasión y salió muy bien. Creo que somos dos jugadores mucho más completos ahora de lo que éramos antes. Confiaría en lo que pudiéramos hacer jugando para el equipo; a los dos nos gusta liderar y mandar para sumar al equipo. Respecto a la alineación real sin mí, antes del Mundial yo hubiese puesto a Goñi y a Juan en el primer turno, porque Goñi tiene un estilo parecido a Leo y cuadraría muy bien con Juan, siendo dos grandes pegadores para aprovechar la bola en ese primer turno. Luego pondría a Arturo como número uno para intentar cerrar con el compañero que elija. Con parejas como las que forman Jon, Yanguas, Paquito, Javi o Coki, tenemos un equipo muy bueno. P: ¿Cuántos Mundiales te quedan por delante? Como decías ya eres un veterano en el circuito. A.G.: Deseo que muchos. El cuerpo dirá lo que aguanta. El pádel es muy longevo y no me imagino el momento de retirarme. En este momento hay que ser más realista que optimista, pero el deseo de que sean muchos está ahí. P: Si proyectamos a medio plazo, están los Juegos Olímpicos de Brisbane 2032 en seis años. ¿Te ves representando a España allí? A.G.: Dependerá del seleccionador y de los jugadores que haya en ese momento, pero yo me veo al mismo nivel. Físicamente, al margen de la lesión, estoy mejor que nunca, y a nivel de pádel también. Ojalá se dé y pueda ser olímpico, es un objetivo más para mantenerme bien físicamente y seguir luchando. P: ¿Sería la guinda del pastel a tu carrera? A.G.: Sería algo grande. Tengo un compromiso muy grande con este deporte y con hacerlo grande. Quiero que sea olímpico porque creo que es algo positivo y el deporte lo merece. Trabajaré para ello y ojalá pueda vivirlo como jugador. Pregunta: Dejando de lado el Mundial, 2026 ha sido un año que ha fluctuado bastante en tu carrera. Empezasteis Fede y tú jugando a un nivel altísimo, por primera vez os pusisteis en la Race con un margen importante con respecto a Tapia y Coello, pero es verdad que desde verano los resultados no han acabado de salir hasta llegar a ese punto que marca la ruptura de la temporada, el torneo de París. ¿Cómo has visto el año? Ale Galán: Honestamente, creo que ha sido el año que más cerca hemos estado y a la vez que el que antes se ha terminado la lucha por el número uno. Siento que ha sido donde en el face to face hemos sido mejores respecto a otros años. Hemos tenido partidos que nunca están ganados, y evidentemente no se ganaron, pero que estaban francamente encaminados e íbamos mandando, como en Valencia o en Burdeos, donde creo que ellos no empezaron del todo bien. Sin duda París marcó el tramo final. En cuanto a resultados no han sido como quisiéramos, pero a nivel de juego creo que ha sido el año en el que mejor hemos estado durante todo el curso. P: En algún tramo de la temporada, cuando hablabas con tu círculo más cercano, ¿llegaste a creer que este año sí? ¿Tuviste ese pálpito? Entiendo que el deportista profesional siempre piensa que tiene opciones o cree en ellas, pero daba la sensación de que podía haber un sorpaso, que podía cambiar la hegemonía del pádel mundial. ¿Sentías que este era el año? A.G.: Lo sentía a finales del año pasado cuando empecé a hacer cuentas, que nunca las hago (se ríe). Y este año sí. En el primer torneo estábamos jugando a un nivel brutal, aunque luego no jugamos a nuestro nivel en la final. De repente ganamos cuatro o cinco veces seguidas y estábamos haciendo las cosas muy bien. Pero bueno, es el deporte: a veces jugando mejor no se cierran las oportunidades, que quizás es una asignatura pendiente nuestra de todos los años. Nosotros generamos más bolas de break que nadie porque somos muy completos y muy intensos, y tenemos que seguir trabajando en cerrarlas para poder amarrar ese tipo de partidos. P: Hay algún punto en la temporada, más allá del Major de París, que para ti haya sido clave y que al echar la vista atrás digas: "Este partido fue clave" A.G.: No, algo más clave que golpeara en lo anímico fue París. El resto hemos ido trabajando y surfeando la ola. En los momentos mejores de juego y, cuando no era tan bueno, seguíamos teniendo esa esencia nuestra de remontar, de estar ahí en los partidos y ganar. No hay un momento tan determinante, pero es verdad que los Majors marcan mucho la temporada y este año no hemos conseguido ganar ninguno, algo que sí habíamos hecho en años anteriores. P: Hablemos de París entonces. ¿Cómo vives ese partido? Para poner en contexto a la gente, en el tercer set teníais una ventaja de 5-2, llegáis a estar a una pelota de tener match point y al final Tapia y Coello acaban remontando, se hacen con el torneo y amplían la distancia en la Race cuando parecía que os ibais a poner por delante. ¿Cómo recuerdas aquello y cómo lo viviste? A.G.: En el momento del partido estaba con las pulsaciones altísimas y no te puedo decir en qué momento tuve la calma para pensarlo, pero en lo anímico posterior ha sido muy duro. Ha sido muy duro porque veníamos de una charla con Jorge porque queríamos darle el número uno, de que Fede ganara su primer Major en París y de que lo teníamos ahí para seguir en esa pelea e ir por delante. Veías tantas cosas positivas... Además, en ese torneo tuvimos el mejor nivel de los últimos dos meses, de principio a fin, desde la primera ronda. Fue duro en lo anímico. Los dos lo notamos, de hecho tuvimos una semana después en la que físicamente nos dio un bajón, no sé si hasta nos pusimos malos, y ya a la semana siguiente pudimos empezar a recuperarnos un poco. P: ¿Llegaste a llorar cuando te fuiste al vestuario con los tuyos y bajó la adrenalina? ¿Te sentiste vulnerable? Teníais el sueño tan cerca después de dos temporadas y media persiguiéndolo… ¿Cómo se gestiona emocionalmente un momento así? A.G.: Te mentiría si te digo que no lo he hecho en alguna ocasión, pero justo esa no fue la del llanto. Era más desconcierto, de tenerlo todo, de cómo habíamos estado luchando, tirando del carro y buscando todas las oportunidades posibles. Fue un poco de desconcierto, de estar desubicado y decir en qué momento se nos ha escapado. Teníamos esas dudas que luego se quedan para los siguientes torneos, el perder esa determinación que siempre tenemos Fede y yo. Estuvimos bastante tocados en lo anímico. Tampoco pensaba que el año estuviera hecho si ganábamos, porque habríamos estado por delante en la Race pero quedaban dos Majors y mucha temporada. Anímicamente habríamos estado en el punto opuesto, con mucha más confianza, pero no con el año hecho. Aun perdiendo en París, si hubiésemos hecho buenos torneos en la gira europea habríamos estado cerca, pero ellos sacaron más distancia ganando allí, por lo que no fue determinante en cuanto a puntos, pero sí en cómo afrontar el resto de la temporada. P: Es obvio que París tuvo un efecto eco porque la gira europea posterior estuvo lejos de vuestro nivel acostumbrado de pisar finales y ganar títulos. ¿Sentisteis que París os desconcertó un poco como al boxeador al que tiran a la lona por primera vez? A.G.: Te compro parte, pero nosotros hemos tocado la lona muchas veces y nos hemos levantado. Diría que somos más como Rocky, buscaremos el premio (se ríe). Pero sí es verdad que generó algo interno, esas dudas de cuando el juego no sale todo lo fluido que quieres. A veces tienes esa determinación y que le vas a dar la vuelta, y así empezó en Róterdam y Düsseldorf contra Stupa y Jon donde teníamos un juego no tan fluido y, cuando parecía que íbamos a remontar, se nos acababa yendo el partido. Se quedaron esos momentos de dudas en los momentos de tensión que a mí me encanta jugar. Han sido muchos torneos seguidos, sin descanso ni apenas tiempo para resetear. Es el deporte que tenemos, que no podemos parar y es competición tras competición. P: Se te ha visto más frustrado y gesticulando más de lo habitual en los últimos torneos. En Milán pareció darse el culmen de no ver en pista al Galán al que estamos acostumbrados. ¿Es algo que tú mismo has detectado y hablado con tu equipo? A.G.: Sí, es verdad. Pero no creo que Milán fuera el culmen, estuve un poco más alicaído en Róterdam y Düsseldorf porque quería reponerme rápido de París y que las cosas salieran rápido que es algo que nunca ha sido el camino con el que hemos encontrado el éxito. Nuestro camino ha sido a base de trabajo y de ser rocosos cuando las cosas no van bien y yo quería ese resarcimiento rápido. He estado más frustrado por ver tan cerca la pelea por el número uno y sentir que se alejaba con ese Major que teníamos en la mano. La sensación era de no tener más oportunidades. Aun así, creo que hemos hecho un gran equipo en los momentos de dificultad. En Milán, tras darme cuenta de que en las semanas anteriores no estuve en mi plenitud, traté de sumar y ayudar. En el último partido, con la carga y molestias que arrastraba, no estaba a mi 100%, pero si tengo que hacer una valoración, fue más positiva que en los dos torneos anteriores. P: Fue precisamente en Milán donde te lesionaste. Se ha especulado mucho sobre tu dolencia y en MARCA informamos sobre cuándo se produjo. ¿Cómo ocurrió la lesión? A.G.: ¿Y según MARCA cuándo se produjo? (se ríe, irónicamente). P: Es en octavos según hemos podido saber. A.G.: Sí, es verdad (se vuelve a reír). Fue en el partido de octavos de final, en una recuperación en un salto, y como yo agarro la pala muy abajo el final de la pala me golpeó justo en la falange donde me hice daño. La pala desestabilizó la falange, noté el dolor y se produjo la rotura. Poco a poco se fue generando más inflamación con el paso de los días. Esos días estuve tratándome, que yo nunca me trato nada del brazo con el fisio y mi foco siempre es recuperar piernas, glúteos y lumbares, y fue extraño decirle a mi equipo que me tratara la mano porque me molestaba. Tomé antiinflamatorios y fue una seguidilla de pequeños pasos para poder competir hasta que, con tanto impacto y tensión, terminó de romperse. P: Simplificando, ¿qué lesión tienes exactamente? A.G.: En el cuarto dedo tengo una lesión de un tejido ligamentoso que tiene que sostener al tendón. Esa rotura hace que el tendón se desplace y genere mucha inflamación y dolor, pero al ser un tejido con poca vascularización no cicatriza como un músculo. Hemos optado por un tratamiento conservador para que vaya recuperando. El paso de las semanas, las pruebas y las resonancias dirán cómo avanza. P: Has comunicado que no estarás en Dubái y por delante sólo quedan Acapulco y el Finals de Barcelona. Sin una fecha concreta de vuelta, ¿vamos a ver a Galán de nuevo en pista en 2026? A.G.: Ojalá, eso quiero. Es una lesión que en deportes de raqueta se ha dado muy poco, los doctores que me tratan me comentario que solo se dio en Matteo Berrettini (tenista) y él pasó por quirófano. No hay plazos ni evidencia muy clara en este deporte que me diga el plazo estimado. No quise arrepentirme de haber desechado esta opción conservadora y deseo recuperarme bien y poder jugar. Si pienso en lo que viene que son Majors, Master Final con muchos puntos…, es lo más interesante para la temporada que viene. Ojalá pueda estar. P: Es decir, ¿no está descartada la operación todavía? Estáis probando este primer tratamiento y según el resultado decidiréis si vuelves, si sigues con el tratamiento o si pasas por quirófano. A.G.: Eso es. De momento estamos en este proceso en el que confío y quiero ser super optimista. Tengo ganas de jugar pero como las inscripciones cierran con tanto tiempo no puedo plantearme una fecha. Quiero seguir haciéndome pruebas para ver cómo me recupero. P: En este periodo fuera, ¿has hablado con Fede Chingotto sobre si él va a competir con otro compañero para mantener el ritmo o si decide esperar a que vuelvas? A.G.: Fede ha sido súper generoso en todo momento. Cuando estuvo sobre la mesa la opción conservadora o intentar jugar con anestesia y operar después, él dijo que lo primero es la salud y lo que nos queda por conseguir. Ha sido muy generoso. Estamos con la expectativa y las ganas de volver a competir juntos, pero estamos en un proceso en el que yo no le puedo garantizar cuándo voy a estar, ni los médicos a mí. P: Al decir "todo lo que nos queda por conseguir", deduzco por tus palabras que por tu cabeza pasa seguir jugando con Fede Chingotto. ¿Se cierra la era 'Chingalan' o no? A.G.: Tendríais que preguntárselo a él, yo me he pronunciado en innumerables ocasiones. La intención es sacar nuestra mejor versión y mantenerlo. Como hemos estado más cerca, lo fácil sería decir "no lo he conseguido, la culpa es de mi compañero", pero el trabajo que hemos hecho nos ha llevado a estar cada vez más cerca. Tengo fe en lo que somos capaces de hacer, en el nivel que hemos dado juntos y en lo que podemos mejorar. Estamos preparando un equipo nuevo para ir a por ello en 2027. P: Hablas de un equipo nuevo. Se anunció que Jorge Martínez deja los banquillos de la élite y ahora hablas de un proyecto propio. ¿Significa que vais a montar una estructura ex profeso para vosotros? A.G.: Es una realidad pública que Jorge no va a seguir viajando en las pistas. Tengo esa ilusión que te da algo nuevo. Ya hemos construido nuestro proyecto y lo sabréis cuando tenga que saberse. Es un equipo nuevo y 'Chingalan' sigue junto en 2027, ahí tienes tus dos titulares (se ríe). P: Te quería preguntar precisamente por Jorge Martínez. Ha sido tu mentor durante 15 o 18 años. ¿Va a ser extraño no verle cada día marcándote lo bueno y lo que hay que mejorar? A.G.: Tengo un gran respeto y admiración por Jorge por todo lo que ha hecho y, sobre todo, agradecimiento. Él me dio la oportunidad a los 15 años y llevo media vida compartiendo equipo con él. Aunque ha sido la cabeza de la estructura, durante 10 años el que me acompañó a diario fue Mariano Amat, pero Jorge siempre estaba cerca aportando, guiándonos y cobijandonos. De Jorge me llevo un aprendizaje en valores y enseñanzas de vida. Admiro mucho el profesional que es y nunca sabré qué hubiese sido de mi vida si no hubiese aparecido. Todo lo que haga en mi vida tendrá una influencia muy marcada por él. P: Sobre Fede Chingotto, ¿tienes la sensación de que se le infravalora a nivel general y no se aprecia el salto cualitativo que ha dado en los últimos tres años? A.G.: Estamos expuestos y leemos de todo, desde que hacen de menos a Fede como a mí. Lo que ha mejorado Fede estos tres años es una bestialidad, tiene un nivel increíble y creo que con la pareja uno somos los cuatro mejores jugadores del mundo por regularidad. Es un hecho que no tiene las aptitudes físicas por estatura o fuerza, pero sigue siendo un jugador mejor que el resto, haciendo finales tres años consecutivos casi todas las semanas y ganando a los mejores sin tener eso que la gente pide. Es increíble que se haga de menos a ninguno de los cuatro con lo que estamos consiguiendo para el deporte. Es una lástima que ahora no se puedan dar estos enfrentamientos. El circuito pierde sin Fede y sin mí en ese sentido o eso espero (se ríe, con naturalidad). P: Has hablado de exposición pública. ¿Tienes la perspectiva de que desde fuera no se conoce del todo a Alejandro, a Alex, y que solo se ve al 'Alien' o al deportista? A.G.: No es una sensación, es una realidad. Es algo que quiero que evolucione. Yo no me identifico con el 'Alien' ni con esa parte pública, solo quiero competir, jugar y ganar cada vez que entro en pista. Trato de ser lo más tranquilo posible, pero disfruto mucho con la gente y creo que en las distancias cortas soy diferente. Creo que se va a ver una imagen más cercana pronto. Durante mucho tiempo he puesto una coraza por miedo a esa exposición siendo más joven, pero ahora quiero empezar a abrirme y abrir las puertas de mi casa. Nunca he subido ni un story de mi casa porque he querido separar mi parte personal de la profesional, pero estoy en un momento donde eso va a cambiar. P: ¿Esa coraza nace tras aquella famosa final de Chile en 2023 y toda la ola de hate que se desató? ¿Te hizo eso alejarte por dolor o inseguridad? A.G.: Venía de antes. Aquello fue un pico alto, pero la polarización empezó antes y ahí intenté mantenerme al margen. Nunca me ha gustado que mi familia pueda contestar o entrar porque sufren y trato de protegerles a ellos más que a mí. Yo doy valor a la gente que entra en mi casa, a mi familia, a mis amigos y a quien me da una crítica constructiva buscando lo mejor para mí. Siempre he intentado proteger a los míos echándome encima y saliendo a dar la cara, como he hecho para reforzar mi compromiso con Fede y darle el valor que tiene. P: ¿Lees redes sociales, mensajes directos o comentarios? ¿Te lo gestiona tu equipo o tienes una cuenta secundaria? A.G.: Tengo un equipo que lleva las redes, pero siempre estoy muy presente en la manera de comunicar y en estar cerca de la gente que me quiere. Estar en pista entrenando y compitiendo es algo que hago por mí, pero solo puedo agradecer todo el cariño recibido de marcas y aficionados. Estoy atento y leo, pero no puedo leerlo todo porque este deporte está creciendo mucho. P: Entonces sí tienes una cuenta secundaria… A.G.: Sí, tengo una cuenta privada para mi gente más cercana. Ahí sí publico cosas de mi casa o mis amigos sin intención de que se vea, también por protección a mi mujer y mi entorno cuando estoy viajando. P: Se te nota más tranquilo y maduro, como si la paternidad y la vida personal te hubiera dado otra perspectiva. ¿Has aprendido a darle su espacio a cada cosa? A.G.: Lo estoy. El objetivo de ser número uno y el hambre siguen siendo voraces, pero ahora disfruto del proceso. Tener esa pasión por lo que hago no dista de tener ese objetivo. Estoy tranquilo porque estoy construyendo una vida más bonita de la que hubiese soñado, estoy creciendo con mi deporte, tengo una mujer maravillosa y una niña que viene en camino. Entiendo que a veces esa sobreprotección de la que hablabámos era solo mis fantasmas. Tengo un gran equipo detrás y mucha ilusión por volver recuperándome bien. P: Si no vuelves a ser número uno, ¿te daría igual? A.G.: No me dará igual no ser número uno porque es mi objetivo al empezar cada temporada, pero seguiré satisfecho con lo que he hecho. Estoy construyendo un legado al margen de los años que sea número uno. Tengo el objetivo de volver a serlo con Fede y creo que es el mejor jugador para arrebatárselo a Agus y Arturo. Además, me gustaría ser el primer jugador en ser número uno en los dos lados. Ya sabéis que me gusta jugar en la derecha y cuando lo consiga con Fede, quién sabe si ese será el siguiente paso. Tengo mucha hambre por conseguir cosas. P: ¿Te planteas realmente pasar al drive en el futuro? A.G.: En menores jugué mucho tiempo en la derecha, empecé el circuito profesional con Javi Redondo en la derecha y en el proyecto con Juan Lebrón la idea inicial era alternarnos en los dos lados. Creo que tengo la capacidad de adaptarme a jugar con todo tipo de jugador y en cualquier lado. Ser el primero en ser número uno en ambos lados es un sueño que me enorgullecería mucho, aunque no es el objetivo a día de hoy. P: En un hipotético proyecto con Galán en la derecha, ¿con quién te gustaría jugar? A.G.: Con el mejor. P: El mejor es Tapia. A.G.: Ahora sí, por supuesto. Pero me estás planteando una pregunta hipotética y quién sabe si cuando me lo planteé el mejor no es, por ejemplo, Manu Castaño, que entreno con él y me gusta mucho cómo juega (se ríe, huidizo). P: Y si tuvieras que elegir a tu jugador favorito de la historia y del circuito actual, ¿quiénes serían? A.G.: Mi jugador favorito de siempre lo he dicho claro, Juan Martín Díaz (se ríe). P: ¿Y de la actualidad? Imagínate que no fueras Ale Galán. A.G.: Del circuito actual no creo que yo fuera mi jugador favorito. No lo sé, me siento identificado con cosas de muchos jugadores del top, pero un jugador que siempre me ha encantado es Lucas Bergamini. Teniéndolo aún más difícil por estatura que Chingo, toca la bola como los ángeles. Admiró también enormemente a Arturo Coello y a Agustín Tapia por cómo juegan y el hambre que mantienen. P: Para acabar, ¿cómo definirías la relación personal entre las dos parejas dominantes del circuito? A.G.: Es buena. El primer año me hacía gracia porque Arturo decía que sentía la necesidad de "odiarnos" en pista para ser número uno, y luego en el Mundial era otra persona. Fuera de la pista hay una relación muy buena entre los cuatro equipos. Al final, los cuatro estamos condenados a entendernos.

articles.title: Tenerife’s Jesus De Miguel honoured in tearful tribute by teammates, fans
articles.summary: Teammates choke back tears, fans chant his name and his family are promised support by the club at the memorial service.
articles.body:
A bouquet of flowers marked the spot on the pitch where Jesus De Miguel fell five days earlier. His teammates returned to the stadium dressed in all black. Above them hung a banner that read “Eterno Demi 9” – Demi 9 forever – a reference to the number nine’s nickname.

In the stands, supporters chanted the name they had once roared to celebrate his goals for CD Tenerife. On Saturday, it was a wail to bid him goodbye.

Thousands gathered at the Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez stadium in Santa Cruz, the capital of Tenerife in the Spanish Canary Islands, where the forward suffered a collision on Monday that resulted in his tragic death . Silence gave way to applause before the club’s centenary anthem was played.

On the makeshift stage, captain Enric Gallego struggled through his farewell speech.

He recalled a teammate so reluctant to inconvenience others that, when his car broke down, he walked home without asking for help.

“To speak of you in the past tense is tremendously unfair,” Gallego said, pausing to regain composure.

“It’s still hard to believe that this has happened to us, Demi, ⁠⁠⁠you’ll always be one of us. We’re still struggling to come to terms with the fact that you won’t be with us again.” ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌

Thundering applause greeted De Miguel’s parents, sister, wife and daughter – a family coping with its loss publicly, but alongside thousands who had gathered to share their grief.

Addressing the bereaved family, Gallego promised that De Miguel’s 18-month-old daughter, Carla, would grow up knowing what her father had meant to those around him.

The club has pledged to financially support Carla until she turns 18.

The solidarity erased the lines of football rivalry across the islands as Ultra Naciente, a supporters’ group from UD Las Palmas in the Canary Islands, placed a wreath on the pitch before the ceremony.

For Jose Diaz Muros, president of Tenerife supporters’ group Pena Iberica, the loss felt personal.

“When a player becomes part of your team, he also becomes part of your life: the conversations at home, the weekends and the memories you share with your family,” he told Al Jazeera.

“That is why a loss like this feels so close, even if you did not know him personally.”

De Miguel’s death was confirmed on Tuesday, hours after he was taken to hospital following a collision with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during Tenerife’s second-division match.

The tragedy has not only brought together football clubs all over Spain, but also raised questions about the response by Spanish football authorities to requests by players for a grieving period.

The Spanish players’ union, AFE, said footballers consulted across the categories unanimously favoured postponement because they did not feel emotionally ready to compete.

Las Palmas defender Alex Suarez expressed that distress publicly: “My head is not in football”.

Three Segunda fixtures were postponed, alongside a women’s match involving Costa Adeje Tenerife, but there was no blanket suspension of games.

The federation’s competition judge ruled AFE’s request inadmissible, saying the decision belonged to La Liga and Spanish football’s top division did not postpone its fixtures.

The governing bodies organised commemorative shirts, floral offerings, pre-match silence and pauses from the ninth minute, honouring De Miguel’s shirt number. Their joint statement presented the tributes as a way to remember him with dignity and respect.

While tributes were paid, AFE’s concerns remained unanswered and football played on.

“There was recognition of the grief, but the collective request was not met in full,” Albert Ortega, a Spanish football expert, told Al Jazeera.

Ortega believes that players’ emotional wellbeing still has less power to alter the calendar than institutional statements suggest. But he cautioned against assuming commercial interests alone explained the decision.

“We cannot demonstrate that money was the only reason for the decision. We can demand transparency about the criteria and the weight given to their views.”

Tenerife fan Diaz Muros acknowledged the difficulties of suspending fixtures, but said players’ concerns should have been addressed.

“Minutes of silence are important, but so is giving people space to grieve.”

In Tenerife, questions were also raised at the resumption of action while an investigation into the collision and emergency response, including treatment and evacuation, were ongoing.

Santa Cruz de Tenerife’s chief prosecutor, Jose Luis Sanchez-Jauregui, told the Spanish news agency EFE that criminal proceedings over the collision seemed unlikely. He cited the distinction between injuries arising during sporting play and deliberate aggression.

Meanwhile, the Spanish football federation’s disciplinary committee has deferred its decision on goalkeeper Owono, but EFE reported a potential suspension of up to 12 matches.

Spanish football expert Ortega argued that prevention of such incidents requires attention that goes beyond individual responsibility.

“Having a written protocol is the starting point,” he said. “Its effectiveness is demonstrated when the people who must implement it know their roles and can act in a coordinated way.”

He proposed independent reviews, regular emergency drills and checks on each stadium’s capacity to respond as possible measures to help prevent such tragedies.

The clash happened during a second division professional football match but questions still remain about procedures in lower division games, where provision of resources and medical response predate De Miguel’s death.

After Colindres goalkeeper Raul Ramirez suffered a fatal injury in the Spanish fifth division in September last year, AFE challenged the provisions in the lower tiers. The ground where he was injured had a defibrillator, but did not have a doctor or ambulance on site.

AFE president David Aganzo has now renewed calls for medical professionals and ambulances across national categories.

According to Ortega, protection also requires a bereavement procedure agreed with players.

Decisions on postponements, the criteria and how teams participate should be made with those stepping on the pitch. Psychological support, he argues, should continue beyond the first week.

For Tenerife fan president Diaz Muros, thoughts must return to those who will continue to grieve for their lifetimes.

“After the tributes, when the attention disappears, they will still be living with that absence. I would like the support to continue then.”

At Tenerife’s Estadio Heliodoro, as the Catholic prayer song Ave Maria played, those gathered stood for a final round of applause.

Above them beamed a monochrome image of Tenerife’s number nine, frozen in celebration, as tears streamed down the faces of his teammates and loved ones.

articles.title: Juanjo Gutiérrez explica por qué dejó a Arturo Coello para el tercer punto de la final del Mundial de pádel
articles.standfirst: El seleccionador español habló tras el quinto título logrado en Doha y su controvertida alineación
articles.summary: El seleccionador español habló tras el quinto título logrado en Doha y su controvertida alineación
articles.body: La selección española volvió a conquistar el trono mundial del pádel masculino después de imponerse a Argentina por 2-1. Un triunfo muy especial para el combinado dirigido por Juanjo Gutiérrez, que puso fin a cinco años de espera y se tomó la revancha frente a su gran rival. Pero, más allá del resultado, una de las grandes decisiones del seleccionador estuvo en la confección de las parejas. La principal sorpresa llegó con Arturo Coello. El vallisoletano, el más dominante del planeta, no apareció en los dos primeros enfrentamientos y quedó reservado para un hipotético tercer partido. Una apuesta arriesgada, ya que existía la posibilidad de que España resolviera la final antes de que el jugador de Valladolid tuviera que saltar a la pista. Gutiérrez apostó inicialmente por Goñi y Lebrón, seguidos de Paquito Navarro y Sanz. Si la eliminatoria llegaba al desempate, Coello formaría pareja con Coki Nieto. Y así ocurrió: ambos fueron los encargados de disputar el punto decisivo frente a Libaak y Alfonso, certificando el campeonato para España. Tras la final, Juanjo Gutiérrez explicó los motivos que le llevaron a tomar esta decisión. En una conversación con 'padelargentinaok', el seleccionador reconoció que disputar el último encuentro de una eliminatoria mundialista supone una exigencia especial para cualquier jugador. "El punto tres le pesa a todo el mundo", reconoció el técnico, que también destacó la capacidad de Arturo Coello para convivir con esa presión. Su criterio a la hora de elegir a los protagonistas no se basa únicamente en el nivel deportivo, sino también en la fortaleza psicológica necesaria para afrontar un escenario de máxima tensión. La decisión terminó saliendo a la perfección. Coello y Coki Nieto respondieron cuando más lo necesitaba el equipo español y se convirtieron en protagonistas de una victoria que devuelve a España a lo más alto del pádel mundial. El seleccionador también asumió el riesgo que implicaba su planteamiento, especialmente después de las críticas recibidas en anteriores ediciones del Mundial. Su estrategia pasaba por anticipar los movimientos de Argentina y distribuir sus jugadores en función de los posibles emparejamientos. En ese sentido, Gutiérrez valoró positivamente su lectura de la alineación rival: "La de Argentina la acertamos al 95%", explicó, señalando que la única diferencia respecto a sus previsiones fue la presencia de Alfonso en lugar de Stupa. Finalmente, el desenlace respaldó la apuesta del técnico español. Una decisión que generó expectación antes de la final y que terminó siendo determinante para que España recuperase la corona mundial.

articles.title: Jaguars to 'listen' to offers for WR Brian Thomas Jr.
articles.summary: With the NFL trade deadline near, Adam Schefter reports that the Jaguars will "listen" to offers for Brian Thomas Jr.
articles.body:
For roughly a year now, trade speculation has surrounded Brian Thomas Jr. However, the Jacksonville Jaguars have remained committed to the talented wideout.

Even for much of this season, with Thomas' role in question, reports have suggested that the Jaguars weren't open to trading him.

But now, with the trade deadline near and opportunities for Thomas limited in the Jaguars' offense, ESPN's Adam Schefter says that Jacksonville will at least "listen" to what other teams have to offer.

"Jacksonville has resisted trade overtures so far, but it sounds like they're going to listen before Tuesday. We'll see if they make a deal," Schefter said on Sunday.

Thomas' fit in Liam Coen's offense has never materialized and this season, his role has continued to shrink as a result. This includes playing just 15 snaps in Week 6 and only 19 snaps in Week 9.

Thomas has also caught just 10 passes this season for 117 yards with two touchdowns. He has three games with no receptions.

However, there are still reasons to keep Thomas as well.

As SI's Albert Breer noted recently, even if the ball doesn't go his way, there is a lot of value that his field-stretching presence adds to the offense. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler pointed out that with the Jaguars in win-now mode, they are looking to add to their roster, not subtract.

It will be up to GM James Gladstone to decide if he'd rather have Thomas' presence on the team, even in a limited capacity, or if he'd rather bank future draft capital to bolster the roster down the road.

articles.title: Antonelli suffers pre-race scare as he spins on way to Sao Paulo GP grid
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli spun on his way to the grid for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix after locking up at the Junção corner ahead of what is set to be a wet race. The Merc...
articles.body:
Kimi Antonelli spun on his way to the grid for the Sao Paulo Grand Prix after locking up at the Junção corner ahead of what is set to be a wet race.

The Mercedes driver managed to get going again and is set to start second alongside pole-sitter Lando Norris.

Antonelli went straight on at the left-hander and spun on the grass as he tried to find traction. He managed to make it back onto the track under his own power.

Junção had already caught out three drivers in Saturday's wet qualifying. Gabriel Bortoleto and Rafael Câmara both hit the barriers there, while Carlos Sainz went off at the same corner in both Q1 and Q2.

Antonelli qualified third on Saturday but was promoted to the front row after Mercedes teammate George Russell received a five-place grid penalty.

articles.title: Kickoff time, TV announced for Iowa State-Cincinnati Nov. 14 game
articles.summary: The kickoff time and TV assignment for Iowa State football's Nov. 14 home game against Cincinnati have been announced.
articles.body:
The hunt for bowl-game eligibility continues for Iowa State football.

The Cyclones' upcoming Nov. 14 home game against Cincinnati will kick off at 11 a.m. CT at Jack Trice Stadium. The Big 12 contest will be televised on TNT.

The game time and broadcast information were announced on Nov. 8.

Cincinnati (5-4, 2-4 Big 12) suffered a 31-24 loss to No. 17 Houston in its most recent game on Saturday, Nov. 7. The Bearcats and Cougars were tied at 24 late into the fourth quarter until Houston's Re'Shaun Sanford II broke loose for the decisive long touchdown run to put Houston in front with 5:10 remaining. The Bearcats were able to cross midfield, but a late turnover sealed their fate.

Cincinnati has lost four of its last five games.

As for Iowa State, the Cyclones squandered a strong start and lost 42-31 at Baylor on Saturday, Nov. 7. Iowa State (4-5, 2-4) is winless on the road but has a 4-1 record at Jack Trice Stadium.

Eugene Rapay covers Iowa State athletics for the Des Moines Register. Contact Eugene at erapay@gannett.com . Follow him on Twitter at @erapay5 .

articles.title: Arizona State QB Jake Fette lives up to hype in first home start
articles.summary: In his first home start for ASU, Jake Fette showed why the coaching staff has been raving about him since got to Tempe.
articles.body:
In August, Arizona State coaches were so eager to see freshman quarterback Jake Fette that they put him in at the end of the team's season-opening 70-7 win over Morgan State. Now, Fette is showing exactly why the coaching staff has been raving about him since he arrived in Tempe.

Fette, who took over the starting role after senior Mikey Keene was injured during the Kansas State game on Oct. 24, shined at times in his official home debut in Tempe. In the Nov. 7 win over Colorado , he flashed his athletic ability and made the precision throws that made him a four-star prospect out of Del Valle High School in El Paso.

But first, it was Fette getting things started at wide receiver.

Out of the wildcat formation with running back Cardae Mack at quarterback, Fette split out to the left and then hauled in a one-yard touchdown pass from Mack to go up 10-0 with 11:15 left in the second quarter. It was the first time that Fette had caught a touchdown pass since he was a junior in high school.

"Oh my gosh, it was crazy," Fette said. "All week they told me, 'Be ready. He might throw it late.' I was like, 'Ah. I don't know. He's going to run it for a touchdown.' And then it actually happened. I didn't even know what to do. I'm just happy I caught it."

Earlier in the scoring drive, Fette showed off his arm talent with a pinpoint throw to wide receiver Omarion Miller down the right sideline for 33 yards to get inside the red zone.

Fette placed the ball on Miller's outside shoulder and hit him in stride.

"The (Omarion) throw really was phenomenal," said coach Kenny Dillingham.

Later in the second quarter, on ASU's next scoring drive, Fette had the throw of the game. Facing a 3rd-and-14, Fette dropped back and connected with wide receiver Reed Harris for a 34-yard touchdown that extended the lead to 17-0 with 2:54 left in the second quarter.

The ball could not have been placed any better, hitting Reed directly in the hands on the right side of the end zone near the sideline.

"The Reed throw was perfectly over the shoulder in that scenario on a third down — critical play," said Dillingham.

Fette is the first ASU quarterback since Jake Plummer (UCLA, Oct. 12, 1996) to have a receiving and passing touchdown in the same game.

Fette, a former high school track athlete and one of the fastest players on the team, made plays with his legs as well.

It was almost as if Fette was growing up in real time on the field in his first start at Mountain America Stadium. He learned from his mistakes, getting the ball out at the right time after taking a bad sack earlier in the game. He made multiple throws that would have NFL scouts — and there were some in attendance at the game — jumping out of their chairs.

It wasn't perfect by any means, with Fette — and the offense as a whole — hitting a wall in the second half and only managing three points. Part of that was due to the conservative playcalling; part of it also fell on the offense. Fette finished the game 13-of-19 passing for 187 yards and one touchdown. But it was a step in the right direction for the youngster.

"I think every game he's going to grow," Dillingham said. "He took a sack on first-and-10. I could hear him on the sideline, 'My fault.' I'm like, 'Settle down. Next play.' I love that. It's all good. Go to the next play. That was the story of the offense tonight.

"The times we got out of sync, there was some sort of play that was a negative and put us way out of sorts. I think for Jake, he did a good job of controlling the game. Once again, stupid things like no penalties, no procedural issues, no 40-second clock, no missed shifts or motioning the wrong guy, very veteran-like operation for a young buck."

The game was a glimpse into the future, which is starting to become increasingly bright in Tempe after a tough stretch in the middle of the season.

The freshman group of Fette, Mack, defensive end Julian Hugo and defensive back Daquwan Dunn is providing a sense of optimism for Sun Devil football.

"This dude's a baller, the way he's handled his business the last few weeks," linebacker Owen Long said. "But not just that, the season since he got here in January. It's been fun to watch. He's been preparing for this moment forever. It's not surprising any of us."

The Detroit Lions have officially announced their inactive players for Sunday's matchup against the Miami Dolphins, and there are a few notable developments.

Seven players will not suit up for Detroit, including cornerback D.J. Reed , edge rusher DJ Wonnum , and center Cade Mays .

However, there's also some encouraging news: Amon-Ra St. Brown is not on the inactive list , meaning the Lions will have their star wide receiver available despite the rib injury that limited him throughout the week.

Detroit Lions Announce 7 Inactive Players

According to the team's official game-day announcement, the following players are inactive against Miami:

The list confirms several absences that were expected entering Sunday.

As previously reported by Detroit Sports Nation , Detroit had already ruled out Mays, Reed, and Wonnum on Friday's final injury report.

However, one notable development is that rookie edge rusher Ahmed Hassanein is inactive, leaving the Lions without another potential defensive-line option.

Detroit will also be without running back Jacob Saylors, who had been listed as questionable with a neck injury.

Amon-Ra St. Brown Active Against Dolphins

The biggest positive from Sunday's announcement involves St. Brown.

After being limited in practice all week with a rib injury, the star receiver is officially available.

As DSN reported earlier Sunday , St. Brown was expected to play despite carrying a questionable designation.

His absence from the inactive list confirms that encouraging pregame expectation.

According to Detroit's official Friday injury report , St. Brown was limited in all three practices leading up to Sunday's contest.

Having him available is a major boost for Jared Goff and a Detroit offense hoping to take advantage of Miami's struggling defense.

The Lions will be shorthanded at several important positions, particularly along the defensive front and in the secondary.

But with St. Brown available and Brian Branch also absent from the inactive list, Detroit gets some welcome reinforcements heading into a game it needs to win.

The Lions must overcome their injuries, maintain their offensive rhythm, and find enough defensive production to leave Miami with another victory.
