articles.title: Social media reacts to Clemson’s tight ACC road win over Syracuse Orange
articles.summary: Here’s a look at how social media reacted to Dabo Swinney and the Clemson Tigers revenge win over Syracuse.
articles.body:
Clemson found another way to win Saturday, even with an offense that never reached the end zone. Behind timely defensive plays and another productive afternoon from Nolan Hauser, the Tigers escaped Syracuse with an 18-13 victory for their second straight road win.

The result moved Clemson to 6-3 overall and 4-2 in ACC play, while giving Dabo Swinney a conference record with his 118th ACC regular-season victory.

Jahiem Lawson supplied the Tigers' only touchdown, returning a backward pass from Steve Angeli 22 yards after pressure from Kourtney Kelly. That third-quarter score created the separation Clemson ultimately needed.

Ashton Hampton later intercepted Angeli in the end zone, wiping out a scoring opportunity with just over six minutes remaining. Syracuse eventually pulled within five, but Tait Reynolds picked up two first downs with his legs to help secure the victory.

Hauser handled the rest of Clemson's scoring with four field goals. His 54-yard make tied the school's single-season record with his 27th field goal and established a program career record for kicks of at least 50 yards.

It was hardly a comfortable afternoon for Clemson, which won without an offensive touchdown for the first time since its 2023 victory over South Carolina. Still, the Tigers head home with consecutive victories and a chance to build momentum against Georgia Tech .

articles.title: Minnetonka eighth-grader is drawing comparisons to Minnesota football legends
articles.summary: A former Gopher believes Theodore Brown could surpass Larry Fitzgerald, Eric Decker and Tyler Johnson as the best wide receivers in Minnesota prep football h...
articles.body:
Theodore Brown might be the next big thing in Minnesota high school sports.

Brown became the first eighth-grader to play varsity football at Minnetonka High School earlier this year, and he's already developed into one of the Skippers' top receivers. His breakout moment came in a thrilling comeback win over Blaine, when he caught two touchdown passes to help Minnetonka advance to the Class 6A state tournament quarterfinals.

Justin Conzemius, a former Gophers defensive back whose son also played at Minnetonka and Minnesota, believes Brown has the potential to become the greatest wide receiver in Minnesota high school history.

"I was there. Watched this kid all year. Potential to be greatest WR in Minnesota high school history," Conzemius posted on X , mentioning Brown alongside Larry Fitzgerald, Eric Decker and Tyler Johnson.

"Amazing body control, hands and football IQ. 8th grade!" Conzemius added.

Putting an eighth-grader in the same conversation as Fitzgerald (Holy Angels), Decker (ROCORI) and Johnson (Minneapolis North) is a bold statement. Fitzgerald, a first-ballot Pro Football Hall of Famer, finished second in the Heisman Trophy voting as a sophomore at Pittsburgh in 2003. Decker and Johnson went on to become two of the most decorated receivers in Gophers history.

Brown certainly gave Minnetonka fans a glimpse of his potential against Blaine, hauling in eight passes for 157 yards and two touchdowns.

The Skippers trailed 21-0 late in the third quarter before mounting a furious comeback. Quarterback Cade Gutzmer connected with Brown for a 37-yard touchdown to cut the deficit to 21-14, then found him again for a 60-yard score with 3:41 remaining to make it 21-20.

Minnetonka completed the comeback with the go-ahead touchdown with just 23 seconds remaining.

Eighth-graders emerging as varsity stars is rare, but Minnesota has seen its share of young phenoms.

Brothers Tyus and Tre Jones made their varsity basketball debuts at Apple Valley High School as eighth-graders, Tyus in 2009-10 and Tre in 2013-14. Paige Bueckers was also an eighth-grader when she debuted for Hopkins High School in 2015-16.

Maddyn Greenway, the daughter of former Vikings linebacker Chad Greenway, began playing varsity basketball at Providence Academy as a seventh-grader. She went on to become a McDonald's All-American and is now in her freshman season at Kentucky.

There's even another eighth-grade football phenom making waves in Minnesota.

Carter Cupito, now a freshman at Blake School, became the starting quarterback at SMB as an eighth-grader. SMB is a co-op program featuring St. Paul Academy, Minnehaha Academy, Blake School and Hope Academy.

The son of former Gophers quarterback Bryan Cupito has already received a scholarship offer from Minnesota, and he'll be back on the field Nov. 12 when SMB faces top-ranked Orono in the Class 4A state tournament quarterfinals.

And while Cupito continues his remarkable freshman season, Brown has an opportunity to add another chapter to his own story when Minnetonka takes the field in the Class 6A state tournament quarterfinals.

It's far too early to know whether Brown will eventually belong in the same conversation as Fitzgerald, Decker and Johnson, but the fact that he's already drawing those comparisons as an eighth-grader speaks volumes about his potential.

articles.title: George Pickens injury update: WRs status revealed 90 minutes before Week 9 kickoff
articles.summary: This is a must-win game for the Cowboys.
articles.body:
George Pickens will not play for the Dallas Cowboys in NFL Week 9, with the wide receiver officially listed as inactive just 90 minutes before kickoff. The late announcement is a significant development for Dallas' offense, which will have to move forward without one of its key receiving options.

Pickens had been listed as questionable heading into Sunday's matchup against the Indianapolis Colts after dealing with a hamstring injury. He was limited throughout the week, leaving his availability in question until the Cowboys released their inactive list.

The Cowboys entered Week 9 hoping Pickens would be available after he managed to practice on a limited basis throughout the week. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer had expressed optimism about the receiver's chances of playing, but that confidence ultimately did not translate into an active roster spot.

Pickens' hamstring issue had kept him from participating fully in practice, and Dallas will now have to adjust its receiving rotation without him. The team had already ruled out KaVontae Turpin, who is dealing with a rib injury, making the receiving situation even more challenging.

Dallas will be without key receiving options

Losing Pickens is a notable setback for the Cowboys as they prepare to face Indianapolis. His absence removes another important option from the passing game, putting additional responsibility on the receivers who are available.

Dallas elevated wide receiver Jordan Hudson from the practice squad ahead of the game, a roster move that could prove especially important with Pickens and Turpin unavailable.

The Cowboys will now have to find production elsewhere as they attempt to navigate a difficult injury situation at wide receiver. Pickens' inactive status is particularly disappointing given the uncertainty surrounding his availability throughout the week and the optimism that he might be able to suit up.

articles.title: AC Milan player ratings vs Genoa: Christian Pulisic sparkles as Rossoneri survive late scare

articles.body:
AC Milan secured a vital 2-1 away victory against Genoa thanks to a clinical first-half blitz. Christian Pulisic and Alphadjo Cisse provided the goals as Ruben Amorim's side climbed the Serie A table.

AC Milan demonstrated tactical superiority in a dominant opening period at the Stadio Luigi Ferraris, effectively deciding the contest within the first twenty minutes. Ruben Amorim's side operated with a fluid 3-4-3 system that overwhelmed Genoa's defensive lines, finding the breakthrough in the 13th minute when Alphadjo Cisse clinical finished following excellent work by Adrien Rabiot. The pressure remained relentless, and just six minutes later, Christian Pulisic doubled the advantage after being teed up by Goncalo Ramos, capping off a sequence of sophisticated positional play.

However, the second half saw a significant shift in momentum as Milan opted for a more conservative block, allowing Genoa to grow into the game. The hosts dominated the shot count 17 to 6, eventually finding a way back through Mikael Ellertsson in the 88th minute. Despite the late tension and a yellow card for Mario Gila during the frantic closing stages, Milan's defensive structural integrity held firm. The victory moves the Rossoneri to 24 points, keeping them firmly in the hunt for the Scudetto following a professional, if eventually nervy, performance.

The Frenchman was the busier of the two goalkeepers, forced into making four saves as Genoa launched a late bombardment. He commanded his area with typical authority, though he could do little to prevent Ellertsson's late strike which took a difficult trajectory. His distribution remained a key facet of Milan's transition play.

Operating on the right side of the back three, De Winter was largely composed during the first half when Milan dominated possession. He faced more scrutiny in the second period as Genoa pushed forward, but he contributed to the team's 15 total clearances to see out the result.

A testing afternoon for the defender who struggled at times with the movement of Genoa's frontline. He received a yellow card in the 87th minute for a cynical foul as the pressure mounted and was caught slightly out of position for the Genoa goal a minute later.

Diawara provided a physical presence in the back three but walked a tightrope after receiving a yellow card in the 29th minute. Amorim recognised the risk of a second booking and withdrew him shortly after the hour mark to ensure Milan finished with eleven men.

Musah's industry was vital in a game where Milan had to absorb significant pressure in the second half. He covered vast ground, aiding the transition from defence to attack, before being substituted late on as Amorim looked to kill the clock.

A dominant performance in the engine room. Rabiot provided the assist for the opening goal in the 13th minute, showcasing his vision and weight of pass. Despite picking up a booking in the 50th minute, he remained the tactical heartbeat of the midfield for the full 90 minutes.

Moreira provided necessary width in the 3-4-3 setup, though his impact faded as the game progressed. He was diligent in his defensive duties, helping to track back when Genoa's wing-backs pushed high in the final half-hour.

The veteran midfielder dictated the tempo during Milan's dominant first half, maintaining a high pass completion rate as the visitors registered 580 total passes. His ability to escape the press allowed Pulisic and Ramos to flourish in the final third.

Cisse set the tone for the afternoon with a composed finish in the 13th minute to open the scoring. His movement between the lines caused constant headaches for the Genoa back three before he was tactical sacrificed in the 61st minute for fresh legs.

The standout performer on the pitch. Pulisic doubled Milan's lead in the 19th minute with a sharp finish and remained the most dangerous outlet for the Rossoneri. Even as Genoa dominated the ball late on, Pulisic's ball retention was crucial before his 79th-minute exit.

While he didn't find the net himself, Ramos was instrumental in the second goal, providing the assist for Pulisic. His hold-up play was excellent, providing a focal point for the attack and allowing the inside forwards to exploit the half-spaces.

Introduced in the 61st minute to provide more defensive stability, he slotted into the system well during a period of sustained Genoa pressure.

Came on for Cisse but struggled to get involved in the game as Milan retreated into a defensive shell for much of his time on the pitch.

A late tactical substitution for Pulisic to shore up the midfield.

Entered the fray in the 87th minute to help defend the lead.

Amorim's tactical setup was perfect for the first 45 minutes, resulting in a two-goal lead. While his side invited perhaps too much pressure in the second half, his substitutions were logical attempts to manage yellow cards and preserve the advantage.

articles.title: Rams-Commanders inactives: Are McDuffie, Curl and Parkinson playing?
articles.summary: The Rams will once again be without Trent McDuffie, as he's inactive today against the Commanders.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams listed five players as questionable to play against the Washington Commanders on Sunday, three of them being key starters. Trent McDuffie is dealing with a back injury, Colby Parkinson has banged-up ribs and Kam Curl picked up a foot injury that limited him in practice.

Additionally, Grant Stuard and Jordan Whittington were also questionable.

The Rams released their list of inactives before kickoff on Sunday, finalizing the statuses of their injured players. McDuffie is officially inactive due to a back injury, but Parkinson is active and will play.

Curl is also active, which is great news for the Rams' safety group. The Rams' other inactives are Joe Cardona, Ty Simpson, Darryl Peterson III, Bill Murray, Keagen Trost and Desjuan Johnson.

The Commanders already ruled out Treylon Burks and Dyami Brown, leaving them thin at wide receiver. Burks is among the team's inactives, but Brown was placed on injured reserve, so that's the reason his name is not on the list.

Fabian Moreau, Isaac Yiadom, Tanoa Togiai and Athan Kaliakmanis are the Commanders' other inactives.

articles.title: Bijan Robinson having big game in Madrid
articles.summary: Robinson's third-quarter touchdown brought the Falcons within a score.
articles.body:
Falcons running back Bijan Robinson is having a big game against the Bengals in Madrid.

With six minutes left in the third quarter, Robinson has 80 rushing yards and 50 receiving yards, and his one-yard touchdown run in the third quarter brought the Falcons to within one score as they trail the Bengals 24-17.

Bengals wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase has been the story of the game so far, but Robinson is also playing very well, as two of the league's best offensive playmakers are putting on a show for an international audience.

As is so often the case with international games played on soccer fields, the footing has been a concern. Several Falcons reportedly changed their cleats to get better traction, and Chase and Joe burrow were seen before the game taking a close look at what appeared to be an uneven part of the playing surface .

But the footing hasn't slowed down Robinson or Chase.

articles.title: Is Emeka Egbuka playing today? Buccaneers injury update for Week 9
articles.summary: The latest on Bucs wide receiver Emeka Egbuka.
articles.body:
Tampa Bay Buccaneers wide receiver Emeka Egbuka has missed the team's last two games with a foot injury that also kept him out of practice Wednesday. But after returning for full practices Thursday and Friday, his status for Week 9 is no longer in question.

Egbuka is expected to play in Sunday night's game against the red hot Chicago Bears , according to multiple reports. His return should help ignite a Bucs passing attack that didn't have a single completion in last week's win over the Falcons and went for just 64 yards the previous week against Carolina.

It'll also be the first time Egbuka and Baker Mayfield play in a game together since Week 3.

Even after missing time, Egbuka remains Tampa's leader in targets, catches and touchdowns. He should be in all lineups against Chicago.
authors: Prince J. Grimes, For The Win

articles.title: Lions inactives: Defense shorthanded vs Dolphins, Amon-Ra St. Brown to play
articles.summary: The Detroit Lions inactives today in NFL Week 9 has them missing several key defenders in their game against the Miami Dolphins.
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions will be without several injured starters today.

The Lions take on the Miami Dolphins in a Week 9 matchup on Sunday, Nov. 8, at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, Florida, entering the game as favorites to win their sixth game of the season. They'll have to do it without several key players on defense, however, with safety Kerby Joseph still unavailable to play after another week of practice.

The Lions will also be without starting cornerback D.J. Reed and edge rusher DJ Wonnum, with Wonnum suffering a concussion in the team's 19-15 win over the Minnesota Vikings last Sunday. Most notably, the Lions will miss injured captain Jack Campbell, who suffered a serious neck injury against the Vikings and was placed on injured reserve on Saturday while he continues his recovery at a Detroit-area hospital.

Notably, receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown and running back Sione Vaki, who both were listed as questionable on the team's Friday injury report, are active for today's game.
